{{short description|Russian theoretical physicist}}
'''Grigory''' (or '''Grigori''' or '''Grigorii''') '''Efimovich Volovik''' (Григорий Ефимович Воловик; born 7 September 1946<ref>[http://www.eduspb.com/node/326 Портал «Санкт-Петербургская школа]</ref> in [[Moscow]]) is a Russian theoretical physicist, who specializes in condensed matter physics. He is known for the Volovik effect.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Bang, Yunkyu|title=Volovik effect in the ±''s''-wave state for the iron-based superconductors|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=104|issue=21|year=2010|article-number=217001|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.217001|pmid=20867127|arxiv=0912.5049|bibcode=2010PhRvL.104u7001B|s2cid=11189974}}</ref>

==Education and career==
After graduating in 1970 from the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]], Volovik became a graduate student at Moscow's [[Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics]], where his received his Russian [[Candidate of Science]] degree (Ph.D.) in 1973. His thesis was on ''Dynamics of a particle strongly interacting with a Bose System''. He has held since 1973 an appointment as a staff member of the Landau Institute and since 1993 a simultaneous appointment as a professor at the Low Temperature Laboratory (now called the Olli Lounasmaa Laboratory) at the [[Helsinki University of Technology]] (now called [[Aalto University]]).<ref name=aps>{{cite web|title=2004 Lars Onsager Prize Recipient, Grigory E. Volovik|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Grigory&last_nm=Volovik&year=2014}}</ref> In 1981 he received from the Landau Institute his Russian [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree (habilitation). His Russian doctoral thesis was on ''Topology of defects in condensed matter''. He is the author or co-author of over 450 research publications.<ref>{{cite web|title=Grigorii E. Volovik, publications|website=Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics, Russian Academy of Sciences|url=https://www.itp.ac.ru/en/persons/volovik-grigorii-efimovich/}}</ref>

Volovik won in 1992 the [[Landau Gold Medal]].<ref name=aps/> He received in 2004 the [[Simon Memorial Prize]] "for his pioneering research on the effects of symmetry in superfluids and superconductors and for extending theses concepts to quantum field theory, cosmology, quantum gravity and particle physics."<ref>{{cite journal|title=Russian physicist scoops low temperature award|website=Physics World|date=25 June 2004|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/russian-physicist-scoops-low-temperature-award/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The London and Simon Prizes|url=http://www.phys.ufl.edu/~lt24/prizes.html|website=24th International Conference on Low Temperature Physics, 10–17 August 2005}}</ref> In 2014 he shared the [[Lars Onsager Prize]] with [[Vladimir Petrovich Mineev]] for "their contribution to a comprehensive classification of topological defects in condensed matter phases with broken symmetry, culminating in the prediction of half-quantum vortices in superfluid [[He-3]] and related systems."<ref name=aps/> Volovik was elected in 2001 a foreign member of the [[Finnish Academy of Sciences|Finnish Academy of Science and Letters]] and in 2007 of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].

Volovik's research deals with low temperature [[quantum spin liquid]]s (such as liquid [[helium]]), [[superfluid]]s, unconventional [[superconductivity]] (''e.g.'' in systems of heavy fermions), the physics of [[glass transition|glasses]] and [[liquid crystal]]s, quantum turbulence, intrinsic [[quantum Hall effect]], coherent states in the [[Larmor precession]]. He proposed ideas and novel experiments to investigate analogies between phenomena of quantum field theory and astrophysics and phenomena of solid state physics.<ref>{{cite journal|volume=351|issue=4|date=September 2001|pages=195–348|journal=Physics Reports|author=Volovik, G. E.|title=Superfluid analogies of cosmological phenomena|doi=10.1016/S0370-1573(00)00139-3|arxiv=gr-qc/0005091|bibcode=2001PhR...351..195V|s2cid=119386265}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Volovik, G. E.|title=Simulation of a Panlevé-Gullstrand black hole in a thin 3He-A film|journal=Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics Letters|arxiv=gr-qc/9901077|year=1999|volume=69|issue=9|pages=705–713|doi=10.1134/1.568079|bibcode=1999JETPL..69..705V|s2cid=23250441}} (See [[Gullstrand-Painlevé coordinates]].)</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Volovik, G. E.|year=2001|title=Fermion zero modes in Painlevé-Gullstrand black hole|journal=Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics Letters|volume=73|issue=12|pages=637–641|doi=10.1134/1.1397745|arxiv=gr-qc/0104088|bibcode=2001JETPL..73..637V|s2cid=15137923}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Volovik, G.E.|year=2021|title=Effect of the inner horizon on the black hole thermodynamics: Reissner–Nordström black hole and Kerr black hole|journal=Modern Physics Letters A|volume=36|issue=24|pages=2150177–2150335|doi=10.1142/S0217732321501777 |arxiv=2107.11193|bibcode=2021MPLA...3650177V|s2cid=236318302}}</ref> He proposed a solution to the problem of the cosmological constant from analogies to solid state physics, in which, unlike particle physics and quantum gravity, the microscopic model is precisely known.<ref>{{cite web|author=Volovik, G.|title=Emergent physics on: vacuum energy and cosmological constant|website=LT-24 talk|url=http://ltl.tkk.fi/wiki/images/7/77/Volovik-LT24talk.pdf}} (talk given at 24th International Conference on Low Temperature Physics in August 2005)</ref> In 2010 with Frans R. Klinkhamer, he published ''Towards a solution of the cosmological constant problem''.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Klinkhamer, F. R.|author2=Volovik, G. E.|title=Towards a solution of the cosmological constant problem|journal=JETP Letters|volume=91|issue=6|year=2010|pages=259–265|doi=10.1134/S0021364010060019|arxiv=0907.4887|bibcode=2010JETPL..91..259K|s2cid=118647860}}</ref>

Volovik collaborated with the experimentalist [[Yury Mikhailovich Bunkov|Yuri Mikhailovich Bunkov]] on the study of particle physics analogues and phenomena in helium-3.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Bunkov, Y. M.|author2= Volovik, G. E.|year=2010|title=Magnon Bose–Einstein condensation and spin superfluidity|journal=Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter|volume=22|issue=16|article-number=164210|doi=10.1088/0953-8984/22/16/164210|pmid= 21386416|bibcode= 2010JPCM...22p4210B|s2cid= 6514650|arxiv=0904.3889}}</ref> In quantum field theory, liquid [[helium-3]] is a good model of the vacuum state in elementary particle physics, with fermions as elementary excitations and bosons such as [[photon]]s, [[graviton]]s, [[gluon]]s as collective ones. According to Volovik's research, excitations and fundamental physical symmetry laws such as gauge and Lorentz invariance are "emergent" laws at sufficiently low temperatures. His view of the emergence of gravitation as a collective vacuum excitation stands in Russia in the tradition of a theory by [[Andrei Sakharov]]. In the case of helium-3, this is expressed by the loss of symmetry at high energies (gas) and the formation ([[emergence]]) of symmetries such as translational invariance in the superfluid state at low temperatures. There are phenomena in between a phase with global U(1) and two SO(3) symmetries and, at even lower temperatures, in the A-phase<ref>{{cite journal|title=Quantized vortices in superfluid <sup>3</sup>He|author=Salomaa, M. M.|author2=Volovik, G. E.|journal=Rev. Mod. Phys.|volume=59|issue=3|pages=533–613|date=July 1987|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.59.533|bibcode=1987RvMP...59..533S}} (over 550 citations)<br />{{cite web|website=IEEE Xplore|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37272168100|title=Martti M. Salomaa}}</ref> additional symmetries which, according to Volovik, are analogous to those observed symmetries (''i.e.'', Lorentz and gauge symmetries and general covariance) of the [[Standard Model]]. Volovik calls the latter phenomenon "anti-[[Grand Unified Theory|GUT]]".<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Volovik, G. E.|title=From analogue models to gravitating vacuum|year=2011|class=gr-qc|eprint=1111.1155}} (See pages 4–5 for introductory remarks on the anti-GUT scheme.)</ref>

He investigated many-body problems from the point of view of classifying their properties as topological defects.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Eltsov, V. B.|author2=Krusius, M.|author3=Volovik, G. E.|year=2005|title=Vortex formation and dynamics in superfluid <sup>3</sup>He and analogies in quantum field theory|journal=Progress in Low Temperature Physics|volume=15|pages=1–137|doi=10.1016/S0079-6417(05)15001-X|isbn=978-0-444-51944-3|s2cid=119079742|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S007964170515001X|arxiv=cond-mat/9809125 |bibcode=2005PrLTP..15....1E }}</ref>  In 2007 he published a Fermi point scenario making the assumption that gravity is "an emergent low-energy phenomenon arising from a topologically stable defect in momentum space".<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Volovik, G. E.|title=Fermi-point scenario for emergent gravity|year=2007|class=gr-qc|eprint=0709.1258}}</ref> He did research on the topological invariants of the [[Standard Model]] and the possible topological [[quantum phase transition]]s that occur between the Standard Model's vacuum states.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Volovik, G.E.|year=2010|title=Topological invariants for standard model: From semi-metal to topological insulator|journal=JETP Letters|volume=91|issue=2|pages=55–61|doi=10.1134/S0021364010020013|arxiv=0912.0502|bibcode=2010JETPL..91...55V|s2cid=62830055}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Volovik, G. E.|author2=Zubkov, M. A.|year=2017|title=Standard model as the topological material|journal=New Journal of Physics|volume=19|issue=1|page=015009|doi=10.1088/1367-2630/aa573d|arxiv=1608.07777|bibcode=2017NJPh...19a5009V|s2cid=118853250}}</ref>

In the first decade of the 21st century he served on the steering committee of the [[European Science Foundation]]'s program Cosmology in the Laboratory (COSLAB).<ref>{{cite web|title=Cosmology in the Laboratory (COSLAB)|website=European Science Foundation|url=http://archives.esf.org/fileadmin/Public_documents/Publications/Cosmology_in_the_Laboratory__COSLAB_.pdf}}</ref>
